output.input_name: Binance in France — screened as BINANCE FRANCE SAS (SIREN 905 060 109)

registration.status: Active in RCS/SIRENE as of 09/11/2026; LEI registration status LAPSED (next renewal 2026-04-20, NON_CONFORMING); removed from AMF PSAN register 2 July 2026 after missing the 1 July 2026 MiCA deadline; winding down — closing all French customer accounts on 31/12/2026

adverse_media.status: Superseded — escalated into a full judicial investigation in January 2025
adverse_media.summary: Paris prosecutor's office opened a preliminary investigation into Binance's French operations for 'illegal' provision of digital asset services and acts of aggravated money laundering (referred to the SEJF financial-crime unit, initially opened Feb 2022 after user complaints); a search/raid of the Paris office was confirmed by CEO Changpeng Zhao

French prosecutors (JUNALCO, Paris financial crime section) opened a full judicial investigation (information judiciaire) before an investigating judge against Binance France for aggravated money laundering, laundering of tax fraud, laundering linked to drug trafficking and illegal exercise of the digital-asset-service-provider (PSAN) profession; facts 2019–2024 in France and across the EU; company denies the allegations and vows to fight any charges
adverse_media.category: Money laundering / tax fraud / illegal DASP activity (criminal investigation)

adverse_media.status: Resolved — plea approved by US District Judge Richard Jones (Seattle) on 23/02/2024 ($1.81bn criminal fine + $2.51bn forfeiture)
adverse_media.summary: Group-level (parent Binance Holdings Ltd, d/b/a Binance.com, Cayman Islands — not Binance France SAS): pleaded guilty in the US to conspiracy to violate the Bank Secrecy Act, failure to register as a money transmitting business and IEEPA violations, agreeing to pay $4.3 billion in penalties and retain a 5-year independent compliance monitor; OFAC simultaneously settled $968,618,825 for 1.67m sanctions violations incl. ~$706m in transactions with users in sanctioned jurisdictions

adverse_media.status: Completed — sentence served; presidential pardon granted 2025
adverse_media.summary: Group-level / UBO (Changpeng Zhao, founder and ~90% owner): pleaded guilty (Nov 2023) to US money-laundering law violations, paid a $50m personal fine and was sentenced to four months in prison (released 27/09/2024); pardoned by President Trump (announced 23/10/2025)
adverse_media.category: Money laundering (individual conviction of beneficial owner)

adverse_media.status: Civil litigation at group level; SEC suit still moving forward in January 2025 (US Supreme Court let investor suit proceed)
adverse_media.summary: Group-level (Binance and Zhao, not Binance France SAS): CFTC lawsuit alleging willful evasion of US law and operation of an illegal digital-asset derivatives exchange; followed by a June 2023 SEC suit against Binance and Zhao on 13 charges of US securities-rule violations
adverse_media.category: Regulatory / securities and derivatives enforcement (US, civil)

adverse_media.summary: Group-level (Binance Holdings Ltd, Zhao and other executives): FTX estate lawsuit seeking nearly $1.8bn over alleged fraudulent transfers related to the July 2021 share repurchase

Tribunal judiciaire de Paris (case 25/54894): a fraud victim who moved scam-proceeds (BTC/ETH) through Binance accounts sought an order compelling Binance France SAS and Nest Services Limited to disclose account-holder data and freeze wallets; the court issued a 'Rejet' (dismissal) on 30 October 2025
adverse_media.category: Litigation — disclosure/freezing request tied to fraud proceeds on platform

adverse_media.status: Confirmed — removal from AMF register on 02/07/2026
adverse_media.summary: Binance France SAS's earlier PSAN registration as a digital asset service provider lapsed: it failed to obtain a MiCA licence by the 1 July 2026 transition deadline and was removed from the AMF PSAN list on 2 July 2026; deposits restricted from 1 July 2026

Binance France is winding down: all French customer accounts close on 31/12/2026; deposits blocked from 29/11/2026; monthly maintenance fee of 0.025% of balance (min 10 USDC) on unwithdrawn assets; trading already ended for French residents; wind-down required by AMF and ESMA under MiCA guidelines
adverse_media.category: Business wind-down / regulatory exit from France

output.risk_rationale: HIGH. Binance France SAS is a registered, active company (SIREN 905 060 109, RCS Paris, LEI 969500IHGTBN0TLO0129 — LEI registration lapsed since 20/04/2026), but it is subject to an ongoing French criminal judicial investigation (opened 28/01/2025 under an investigating judge at JUNALCO) for aggravated money laundering, laundering of tax fraud, laundering linked to drug trafficking and illegal DASP activity — directly against the screened entity. Its beneficial-owner chain reaches Changpeng Zhao (~90% of the group), who was convicted of US money-laundering violations in 2023–2024 (later pardoned in Oct 2025) and is PEP-flagged in OpenSanctions with government advisory roles; the parent Binance Holdings Ltd took a record $4.3bn US criminal resolution including a $968.6m OFAC sanctions settlement, with a 5-year compliance monitor. Screening returned no match on OFAC SDN, UK OFSI or EU consolidated lists for either the entity or its owners, and no PEP status for the local directors (David Prinçay, Christelle Tang). Compounding the risk, the entity lost its French PSAN authorisation on 02/07/2026 after missing the MiCA deadline and is now winding down all French accounts by 31/12/2026 — an exit driven by regulatory failure rather than ordinary commercial closure.
